P1.evidence: Setter notes used well and specifically - 'I was talking with Kyla that you spoke the other day... that you had some amazing goals. You have seven grandkids' and later 'Do I had it correctly that your handicap is six in golf?' But no frame was set at all. The rep asserted the agenda instead of agreeing it - 'we're meeting today because you're not complacent with where you're at right now' - and never asked what the prospect was looking for help with.

P2.evidence: Age known, weight asked directly ('you're 67 today. How much do you weigh?'), height volunteered. Dentistry probed intelligently - 'I think I had at least three or four calls like this with dentists. Every single one was complaining about back pain issues' - which surfaced the disc surgery. Injuries chased in detail including 'The shoulder injury, does it appear in every day right now?' and the cross-legged floor-rise test. Diet worked meal by meal. But diabetes and the TRT history both arrived unprompted under the nutrition question, sleep was never asked, and energy only came up inside the TRT story.

P3.evidence: Strongest goals work in the batch on the physical layer - 'Any other goals that you want to hit?', the toe-touch and floor-rise probes, and 'what becomes possible when you're actually getting stronger, having more energy throughout the day? Like, what opens up for you?' The grandchildren thread was driven all the way to identity - 'That's the super grandpa that we're addressing' - and reflected back at the price drop. Marked down because the rep supplied the grandchildren driver ('you seem like a guy that wants to be active in your grandkids life') rather than asking for it.

P4.evidence: 'What was the reason that you've been, like, falling off?' produced the whole history - kids' activities, golf, bowhunting, 600 acres. Then 'what do you feel is still missing? Or where you feel that you're potentially leaving something on the table?' got the gap in his own words: 'I'm kind of cobbling together a routine... there's no rhyme or reason to it. It's just kind of a shotgun approach.' The information-isn't-the-problem move never ran.

P5.evidence: One real consequence beat, and a good one: 'if your dad is 91, that's definitely that's your future... And that's a good news and a bad news at the same time. Because being 91 and being crippled, it's no fun.' Nothing after it - no two-year horizon, no 'is that something you're willing to settle for', no 'why not', no line in the sand. On a 67-year-old with diabetes and a disc history this was the phase with the most available material and it was left on the table.

P6.evidence: 'If you had this right training, structured, right nutrition, and accountability from Trevor all built around your lifestyle, do you agree that you would get to your physique that you want?' then 'if we can figure out all the details, are you fully committed to actually showing up and doing the work to become that new version of Matt?' Answer was clean: 'Oh yeah, yeah... I don't see myself taking it on and not continuing following through with it.' Marked down only in the coach note because it ran after the pitch, not before.

P11.evidence: Price was presented but no payment step was reached - the prospect deferred to his wife and the call ended on a plan to schedule a joint call. No deposit was requested, despite the manager instructing the team three days earlier that spouse objections should be met with a deposit.

objection_plays.detail: Best-run play in the batch. Money-aside tie-down ('let's put that money aside for a second, you personally feel that this can get you to your goals?'), the why behind the belief ('What specifically feels for you that you can?'), obstacle-mapping ('when you're going to talk to Paige, what do you feel the potential obstacles might be?'), and the she-would-not-oppose-you check ('it's not that you're, she would be like opposed of, for you getting in a better...'). He also pre-scripted the conversation she will have and offered the joint call. Two moves did not run: the permission-versus-input challenge ('is this genuinely needing her input, or asking permission to bet on yourself?') and the deposit-with-refund fallback, which is exactly what the manager had told the team to use here.

Opened correctly - 'if you would be open to just have an open conversation about finances, we can talk about it, like how we can actually work around that so it would be digestible for your household' - and asked cash on hand, establishing $50,000 available and that the constraint is cash flow, not funds. Then it stopped. No monthly surplus, no cards, no available credit, no investments, and crucially no plan was ever presented, despite the rep having promised 'this is how much it is, but we can do it like this, this, or this way.' He sent the prospect to his wife with only the full $6,000 number in hand - the exact failure mode the rep himself had just described.

'It's just a matter of, is this the right timing?' landed clearly and no OD move ran - no 'things never slow down', no compounding cost of waiting, no 'the only thing you can control is right now'. On a 67-year-old this was the most persuasive available play.

notes: Excellent discovery, an exemplary spouse play, and a clean commitment yes - then the money conversation stopped halfway and he was sent home with an unpriced $6,000 and no deposit. Finish the open wallet and put a concrete plan in his hand before the joint call, and take the refundable deposit the manager has been asking for.
